task_instance: Bootstrap a brand-new minimal WinUI 3 app named 'HelloWinUI' using the skill's setup-and-scaffold flow: run `dotnet new winui -o HelloWinUI`, build it with `dotnet build`, and launch it to confirm a real top-level window appears.
blocker_detail: WinUI 3 / Windows App SDK is a Windows-only desktop GUI framework. The runtime is Linux (uname: Linux 6.18.44-fc-v37, x86_64), so there is no Windows OS, no `winget` (used by the skill's bundled config.yaml to install Visual Studio 2026 and Windows App SDK components), and no Windows XAML compiler / windowing subsystem to build or launch a WinUI top-level window. `dotnet new list winui` on the available .NET 8 SDK returns 'No templates found matching: winui' because the WinUI 3 project templates ship only via the Windows-targeted Visual Studio/Windows App SDK workload, not as a cross-platform dotnet template package. Attempting to fetch it from NuGet also failed because the sandbox's egress proxy blocks NuGet/Azure package feeds (pkgs.dev.azure.com, azuresearch-ussc.nuget.org) by organization policy. Even absent that network restriction, WinUI 3 apps fundamentally require a Windows runtime to compile XAML and render a native window, which this Linux container cannot provide, and provisioning/using a Windows machine is outside what this runtime grants (no ability to run a Windows OS or GUI here). The core deliverable of the skill (scaffold, build, and launch a real WinUI 3 window) is therefore unreachable in this environment.
evidence: Ran `uname -a` -> Linux 6.18.44-fc-v37 (no Windows). Confirmed `dotnet --version` -> 8.0.131 present but generic .NET SDK, no `winget` binary on the system (`which winget` returned nothing). Ran `dotnet new list winui` inside a scratch test dir -> exit code 103, 'No templates found matching: winui', with the agent proxy log showing outbound connections to pkgs.dev.azure.com and azuresearch-ussc.nuget.org (NuGet feeds needed to fetch the WinUI project template) rejected by organization policy. No WinUI project, build, or running window was produced.
